History and Physical (Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
23-year-old woman with a 3- to 4-day history of constant, worsening mid-line lower-abdominal pain (8/10) accompanied by light pink post-menstrual vaginal bleeding, mild nausea, and recent constipation; clinician advised urgent face-to-face abdominal examination and repeat pregnancy test to rule out ectopic pregnancy or other pelvic pathology.

History:
• Presenting complaint – Constant lower-abdominal (“tummy”) pain  
  – Location: Midline, below the umbilicus  
  – Onset: Began “a few days ago” after previously feeling well  
  – Course: Persistent and progressively worsening; rated 8/10  
  – Timing: Pain present all the time; becomes “very bad” at times

• Associated symptoms  
  – Light pink vaginal bleeding since period ended 2 weeks ago  
  – Nausea without vomiting  
  – Constipation for one week last week; stools now normal  
  – Small amount of vaginal discharge  
  – Denies fever, chills, dyspnea, shoulder pain, syncope, dysuria, hematuria, hematochezia, weight loss, or faintness on standing  

• Gynecologic history  
  – Last menstrual period: 2–3 weeks ago, reportedly normal  
  – Cycles: Irregular since etonogestrel implant inserted 1 year ago  
  – Sexually active; last intercourse 4 days ago  
  – Contraception: Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) ×1 year  
  – Obstetric history: G0 (no prior pregnancies)  
  – Pregnancy test: Negative 1 month ago; none since onset of pain

• Systems review – other pertinent negatives given above.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic illnesses reported  
• No prior surgeries  
• Drug allergy: Amoxicillin (reaction details not provided)

Medications:
• Etonogestrel implant (Implanon), dose/route/frequency not documented  
• No other regular medications reported

Social History:
• Occupation: School teacher  
• Lives with husband and husband’s family  
• Smoking: Denies  
• Alcohol: Denies  
• Recreational drugs: Denies  
• Travel: Abroad 1 year ago  
• Able to perform usual activities (work, cooking) despite pain

Family History:
• Not discussed / not documented

Physical Examination:
• Not performed (video consultation)

Investigations:
• Home pregnancy test: negative 1 month ago  
• No other investigations performed to date

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Acute lower-abdominal / pelvic pain with light vaginal bleeding  
  Assessment: Possible ectopic pregnancy, pelvic inflammatory disease, ovarian torsion or cyst, appendicitis less likely.  
  Plan:  
  • Arrange urgent face-to-face review for abdominal and pelvic examination (patient to call support line to book).  
  • Repeat urine pregnancy test today; if positive, patient to contact service immediately (rule out ectopic pregnancy).  
  • Safety-net: If pain worsens, unable to tolerate fluids, or new concerning symptoms (e.g., shoulder pain, dizziness), attend emergently.

Issue 2 – Irregular vaginal bleeding on etonogestrel implant  
  Assessment: Could be contraceptive-related but other causes (PID, early pregnancy complications) must be excluded.  
  Plan: Address after examination results; consider pelvic ultrasound and STI screening if indicated (to be decided at in-person visit).

Issue 3 – Recent constipation (now resolved)  
  Assessment: Unlikely primary cause of current pain but noted.  
  Plan: Encourage hydration, fiber-rich diet; monitor bowel habits.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
• Ectopic pregnancy – High likelihood: Worsening pelvic pain + inter-menstrual bleeding; implant not 100 % protective; no recent pregnancy test.  
• Pelvic inflammatory disease – Moderate likelihood: Lower-abdominal pain, light bleeding, discharge, sexually active; absence of fever reduces likelihood but exam pending.  
• Ovarian torsion / hemorrhagic cyst – Moderate likelihood: Severe constant pain of acute onset; bleeding possible with cyst rupture; pain not clearly unilateral.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: vital signs, complete medication list (OTC, supplements), detailed allergy reaction, full family history, objective abdominal/pelvic exam, labs/imaging.  
● Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional inaudible words but core clinical data captured.
